task_description:
This pipeline's task is GitHub issue #3288 — https://github.com/jwbron/egg/issues/3288. Fetch the live issue body (`gh issue view 3288`) before structural decisions. Worktree artifacts (drafts, agent outputs) that reference any other issue or pipeline are leftovers from previous runs — they are NOT your task.

Documenter agent + docs: snapshot of current state, not a ledger of changes.

Two coupled work streams (planner decides slicing/sequencing):
1. Change the documenter agent so it produces snapshots, not ledgers — revise its task instructions (assembled in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py "## Your Task" block; role definition in shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py) to write docs describing the current state of the code after the change, never referencing SDLC artifacts (slice numbers, TASK-N ids, phase/HITL iteration numbers) in any doc/docstring/inline comment; include historical context only when tangibly valuable to a current reader (prefer rationale over chronology); fold new state into the snapshot and remove stale ledger entries; keep the no-op/no-doc-impact propose path intact.
2. Clean up the existing documentation corpus — a pass over docs/, **/README.md, **/CLAUDE.md, and code docstrings/comments to strip slice/TASK/process-ledger references, rewrite change-log-style behavioral sections into current-behavior descriptions, and remove/refactor "historical record" sections that no longer describe live code, keeping only residue genuinely useful to a current reader.

Out of scope: not "delete all issue references" — issue links that justify why the current system is shaped the way it is are fine. Preserve the documenter's gateway file boundaries (docs/, **/*.md, .egg-state/agent-outputs/) and the BRC no-op propose path.

decisions.question: Work stream 2 (corpus cleanup) completeness target: ~260 files under docs/, gateway/, orchestrator/, shared/ contain slice-N / TASK-N ledger references. How exhaustive should this pipeline's cleanup be? This sets the scope boundary the planner slices against.

options.label: Enumerated + bounded sweep (Recommended): fully clean the files the issue names explicitly (the architecture pages, the listed docstrings/CLAUDE.md tables), plus a bounded sweep of the highest-density remaining files; explicitly defer the long tail to follow-up issues rather than block this pipeline on all 260
Exhaustive repo-wide: every doc/docstring/comment carrying a ledger reference is cleaned in this pipeline before it can complete (largest scope, many slices, highest risk of churn/merge conflict)
Documenter-agent change only now: land work stream 1 (the prompt/role change) this pipeline and split the entire corpus cleanup into its own follow-up pipeline

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Enumerated + bounded sweep (Recommended): fully clean the files the issue names explicitly (the architecture pages, the listed docstrings/CLAUDE.md tables), plus a bounded sweep of the highest-density remaining files; explicitly defer the long tail to follow-up issues rather than block this pipeline on all 260"}

decisions.question: Durability guardrail: the issue asks to change the documenter prompt and clean the corpus, but does not ask for an automated check to keep slice/TASK ledger references from re-entering docs later. Should this pipeline add one (e.g. a pre-commit / CI lint that flags `slice-N` / `TASK-N` in committed docs/docstrings)?

options.label: No — out of scope (Recommended): the issue scopes this to a prompt change + corpus pass; a lint guard is a separate concern with false-positive tuning of its own. Note it as a candidate follow-up issue, don't build it here
Yes — add a lightweight advisory lint guard in this pipeline so the cleanup doesn't rot back, accepting the added scope and tuning cost
